planting.note: Set out transplants after all danger of frost into lean, well-drained soil in full sun; this compact selection is usually grown from nursery starts rather than seed.

directions: This dwarf selection of tall verbena keeps the same wiry stems and lavender-purple flower clusters as the species but on a shorter, denser, rounded mound about a third the height, so it holds its shape at the front of a border or in a large pot instead of towering and flopping. Plant in full sun in average to poor, sharply drained soil; like the species it is drought-tolerant once rooted in and blooms almost continuously from late spring to frost, drawing butterflies and bees the entire time. It rarely needs staking thanks to its compact habit, but a light shearing after the first flush encourages denser rebranching and heavier repeat bloom. Hardy as a perennial from about zone 7 south; elsewhere it self-sows or is treated as an annual.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, since this was bred as the first true seed-grown Spanish lavender; transplant out after frost into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun.

directions: Bandera Purple was bred as one of the first Spanish lavenders reliably grown from seed, producing a uniform, compact mound topped with dense flower cones in deep purple crowned by showy purple flag bracts. Sow indoors and grow on cool and bright to avoid legginess, then transplant into lean, gritty, well-drained soil in full sun once frost danger has passed. Its dwarf, tidy habit suits containers and small-garden borders better than larger stoechas types, and it tends to flower earlier in its first season than cutting-grown cultivars. Water only when the soil has dried and avoid rich soil or heavy mulch, both of which invite root rot in this drought-adapted plant.

scientific_name: Lavandula stoechas subsp. stoechas f. rosea 'Kew Red'

planting.note: Transplant nursery-grown starts after last frost into lean, sharply drained, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; this cultivar does not come true from seed and is propagated by cuttings.

directions: Kew Red stands apart from most Spanish lavenders for its distinctive coloring: deep pink-red flower cones topped with pale, almost white flag bracts that flutter above the blooms like small wings. It forms a well-branched, compact, free-flowering bush and blooms earlier and more heavily than many stoechas cultivars, repeating well if deadheaded. Grow in full sun in lean, gritty, sharply drained soil, since it shares the family's intolerance of wet feet and humid, heavy clay. Shear lightly after each flush to maintain a dense shape and prevent the woody, splayed-open habit lavenders develop with age.

planting.note: Transplant rooted starts after last frost into lean, well-drained soil in full sun; propagated by cuttings rather than seed.

directions: Ballerina produces plump purple flower cones topped with long-lasting bracts that open white and slowly fade through pink to purple as they age, giving each spike a two-tone, aging-in-place look over several weeks. The aromatic silvery foliage and rounded habit make it a good match for mass plantings, low informal hedges, and containers. Plant in full sun in well-drained, on the leaner side of average soil, and let the soil dry between waterings once the plant is established, since overwatering is the most common cause of failure. Deadhead spent spikes to prolong the mid-spring through late-summer bloom period.
